answer: The sawyer rips his oak bolts into staves, and the rip must follow the grain or the stave cups in the sun. Stave elm bung maker croze bond governs the ripping: a bond elm bung makers lodge after bung bench inspections. First comes the karst, ripped at the sawpit; then the terrace, ripped before the bolts run out; the island is the sawpit itself, deep with sawdust. A cheat must rip 67 false bolts and fill 67 false sawpits.
